$$

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(P∨Q)∧¬(P∧¬Q) & ≡(\text{T}∨\text{F})∧¬(\text{T}∧¬\text{F}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∧¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}∧\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{F}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(P∨Q)∧¬(P∧¬Q) & ≡(\text{F}∨\text{T})∧¬(\text{F}∧¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∧¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}∧\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬(P∨Q)\,$ | $\,¬P∨Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-3}} | $\text{T}$ |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

¬(P∨Q){{field-4}}¬P∨Q
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(P∨Q) & ≡¬(\text{T}∨\text{T}) \\  & ≡¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬P∨Q & ≡¬\text{T}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{F}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(P∨Q) & ≡¬(\text{F}∨\text{F}) \\  & ≡¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,¬(P∨Q)\,$ | $\,¬P∨Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

To determine whether $¬(P∨Q)$ is logically equivalent to $¬P∨Q,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are *different* (one is $\text{F},\text{F},\text{F},\text{T}$, while the other is $\text{T},\text{F},\text{T},\text{T}$). Therefore, we conclude that 

$$

Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∧(B∨¬A)\,$ | $\,A∧B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
A∧(B∨¬A){{field-4}}A∧B
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A∧(B∨¬A) & ≡\text{T}∧(\text{T}∨¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∧(\text{T}∨\text{F}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∧\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A∧B & ≡\text{T}∧\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{F}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A∧(B∨¬A) & ≡\text{F}∧(\text{T}∨¬\text{F}) \\  & ≡\text{F}∧(\text{T}∨\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{F}∧\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A∧(B∨¬A)\,$ | $\,A∧B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

To determine whether $A∧(B∨¬A)$ is logically equivalent to $A∧B,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.  

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are the same $(\text{T},\text{F},\text{F},\text{F}).$ Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
A∧(B∨¬A)≡A∧B.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬(A∧¬B)\,$ | $\,¬A∨B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
¬(A∧¬B){{field-4}}¬A∨B
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(A∧¬B) & ≡¬(\text{T}∧¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡¬(\text{T}∧\text{F}) \\  & ≡¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬A∨B & ≡¬\text{T}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{F}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(A∧¬B) & ≡¬(\text{F}∧¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡¬(\text{F}∧\text{F}) \\  & ≡¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below. 

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬(A∧¬B)\,$ | $\,¬A∨B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

To determine whether $¬(A∧¬B)$ is logically equivalent to $¬A∨B,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are the same $(\text{T},\text{F},\text{T},\text{T}).$ Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
¬(A∧¬B)≡¬A∨B.
$$

$$

First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B) & ≡(\text{T}∧\text{T})∨¬(\text{T}∨¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡(\text{T}∧\text{T})∨¬(\text{T}∨\text{F}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∨¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B) & ≡(\text{T}∧\text{F})∨¬(\text{T}∨¬\text{F}) \\  & ≡(\text{T}∧\text{F})∨¬(\text{T}∨\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{F}∨¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{F}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B) & ≡(\text{F}∧\text{T})∨¬(\text{F}∨¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{F}∨¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

To determine whether $(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B)$ is logically equivalent to $A,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

We see that the columns for $(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B)$ and $A$ are different. They differ in the second and third rows. Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B)≢A.
$$

tutorials.problem:
Two statements are **logically equivalent** if they have identical truth values in their respective truth tables. In this lesson, we'll use truth tables to show that two complex compound statements are logically equivalent. 

If two statements $P$ and $Q$ are logically equivalent, we write

$$
P\equiv Q
$$

where the symbol "$\equiv$" means "is logically equivalent to."

For example, let's use a truth table to prove the following logical equivalence:

$$
(A \land \neg A) \lor B \equiv B
$$

First, we construct truth tables with columns $A$ and $B$ containing all possible combinations of truth values. Then, we create another column for $\neg A,$ which has the opposite truth values to $A.$

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\, \neg A \,$ |

| $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm F}$ | $\textrm T$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm T}$ |
| $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm F}$ | $\textrm F$ | $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textrm T}$ |

Now, we add a column for $A \land \neg A.$ Recall that $A\land \neg A$ is true if $A$ is true and $\neg A$ is true and is false otherwise. In this case, $A\land \neg A$ is always false.

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\, \neg A \,$ | $\, A \land \neg A \,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
